clinician.final_diagnosis: diffuse fibrinous peritonitis with no obvious perforation of abdominal viscus
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old G2P2 female presented nine days post-partum with a three-day history of nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramping, profuse diarrhea, lower abdominal pain, and fever. Initial examination revealed tachycardia (HR 124), fever (39.4 C), and a soft, tender abdomen with mild guarding and suprapubic tenderness. Laboratory results showed signs of inflammation (elevated bands, platelet count) and electrolyte imbalances. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis revealed an enlarged post-gravid uterus, bowel wall thickening, and a large fluid collection superior to the spleen. The patient was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics (ceftriaxone, ampicillin, clindamycin, gentamicin). Due to persistent symptoms and imaging findings, a diagnostic laparotomy was performed, which confirmed diffuse fibrinous peritonitis with no obvious perforation of abdominal viscus. Postoperative cultures were negative, possibly due to prior antibiotic treatment. The patient continued to experience persistent tachycardia and fever, with concern for endometritis and colitis. A repeat CT one week postoperatively showed a significantly decreased volume of the fluid collection.
